mcqs.q: On a slide, the stage of tooth development is recognised mainly by:
opts: The shape of the enamel organ and the structures present
The colour of the stain only
mcqs.explain: Stages are identified by the shape of the enamel organ (bud/cap/bell) and which structures (papilla, sac, layers) are present.

mcqs.q: This slide shows a rounded epithelial bud off the dental lamina — the:
mcqs.explain: A rounded epithelial bud (enamel organ) with surrounding condensing ectomesenchyme is the bud stage.

mcqs.q: A cap-shaped enamel organ with a visible dental papilla and dental sac indicates the:
mcqs.explain: In the cap stage the enamel organ is cap-shaped and the dental papilla (below) and dental sac (around) become visible.

mcqs.q: The cuboidal cells along the CONVEX border of the enamel organ are the:
mcqs.explain: The outer enamel epithelium is the cuboidal layer covering the convexity of the enamel organ.

mcqs.q: The tall columnar cells on the CONCAVITY (future ameloblasts) are the:
mcqs.explain: The inner enamel epithelium (tall columnar pre-ameloblasts) lines the concavity and forms enamel.

mcqs.q: The star-shaped cells filling the centre of the enamel organ are the:
mcqs.explain: The stellate reticulum is the central network of star-shaped cells.

mcqs.q: The ectomesenchyme enclosed BELOW the enamel organ (forming dentin/pulp) is the:
mcqs.explain: The dental papilla lies within the concavity of the enamel organ and forms the dentin and pulp.

mcqs.q: The ectomesenchyme ENCIRCLING the tooth germ (forming the periodontium) is the:
mcqs.explain: The dental sac encircles the enamel organ and papilla and forms the periodontium (cementum, PDL, bone).

mcqs.q: The transient strand of cells associated with the enamel knot, marking the first cusp, is the:
mcqs.explain: The enamel cord is a transient strand of cells (with the enamel knot) thought to mark the position of the first cusp.

mcqs.q: In the ADVANCED bell stage, you would expect to see:
opts: Ameloblasts and odontoblasts depositing the first hard tissue
mcqs.explain: The advanced bell stage shows differentiated ameloblasts (from IEE) and odontoblasts (from papilla) laying down enamel/dentin at the future DEJ.

opts: Localized proliferation within the dental lamina of each primary tooth germ
A posterior extension of the dental lamina
mcqs.explain: Successional (permanent) teeth form by proliferation within the dental lamina associated with each primary tooth germ.

mcqs.q: Accessional teeth (the permanent molars) form from:
opts: A posterior extension of the dental lamina
mcqs.explain: Accessional teeth (permanent molars) form as a posterior (distal) extension of the dental lamina.

mcqs.q: The early bell stage is recognised on a slide by:
opts: A bell shape with four cell layers and no hard tissue yet
mcqs.explain: Early bell shows a bell-shaped organ with four layers (OEE, IEE, stratum intermedium, stellate reticulum) before any hard tissue forms.

mcqs.q: Ameloblasts (enamel-forming cells) are derived from the:
mcqs.explain: Ameloblasts differentiate from the inner enamel epithelium.

mcqs.q: Odontoblasts (dentin-forming cells) are derived from the:
opts: Peripheral cells of the dental papilla
mcqs.explain: Odontoblasts differentiate from the peripheral cells of the dental papilla, under inner-enamel-epithelium influence.

mcqs.q: Which structure separates the cap-stage enamel organ from the dental lamina?
mcqs.explain: In the cap stage, the enamel organ has a short, broad connection (stalk) to the dental lamina.

mcqs.q: Which sequence correctly orders the morphological stages?
opts: Bud → cap → early bell → advanced bell
mcqs.explain: The correct order is bud → cap → early bell → advanced bell (with formation of enamel/dentin matrix).

mcqs.q: The dental sac on a slide is best located:
mcqs.explain: The dental sac (follicle) is the ectomesenchymal condensation encircling the entire tooth germ.

saqs.q: How do you tell the bud stage from the cap stage on a slide?
saqs.a: Bud: a rounded epithelial bud with condensing ectomesenchyme. Cap: cap-shaped enamel organ with a visible dental papilla (below) and dental sac (around).

saqs.q: Name the three enamel-organ layers and the cells of each.
saqs.a: Outer enamel epithelium (cuboidal, convexity), inner enamel epithelium (tall columnar, concavity → ameloblasts), stellate reticulum (star-shaped central cells).

saqs.q: What do the dental papilla and dental sac form?
saqs.a: Dental papilla → dentin and pulp. Dental sac → periodontium (cementum, PDL, alveolar bone).

saqs.q: What is seen in the advanced bell stage?
saqs.a: Differentiated ameloblasts (from IEE) and odontoblasts (from papilla) depositing the first dentin/enamel at the future DEJ.

Successional: form by proliferation within the dental lamina of each primary germ (permanent incisors/canines/premolars). Accessional: permanent molars from a posterior extension of the dental lamina.

saqs.q: From which layers do ameloblasts and odontoblasts arise?
saqs.a: Ameloblasts from the inner enamel epithelium; odontoblasts from the peripheral cells of the dental papilla.

saqs.q: What is the enamel cord and its significance?
saqs.a: A transient strand of cells (with the enamel knot) extending toward the OEE; it helps mark the position of the first cusp during crown formation.
